target_label: SAP Certified - Implementation Consultant - SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition - Sales
purpose: SAP Learning defines the syllabus boundary. Our units go deeper: understand the mechanism, apply it to a concrete case, explain it without notes, and keep evidence of competence.

mastery_scale.3: Explain, apply, and handle a changed example without the article open

units.understand: Reconstruct sell-from-stock end to end and separate order decisions from later ATP, delivery, goods issue, billing, and accounting events.
units.apply: Trace one order with a split confirmation and partial delivery; mark the document, status, organizational data, and master data consumed at each step.
units.explain: Explain what the sales order commits to and what is still determined or executed later.
units.evidence: A flow plus one changed-case explanation showing the first control that changes.

units.understand: Understand quotation validity and follow-on/reference behavior without treating a quotation as an executable customer order.
units.apply: Compare a quotation that becomes an order with one that expires or is rejected; identify copied versus redetermined data.
units.explain: Explain why a quotation is not a sales order and what evidence proves conversion.
units.evidence: A quotation-to-order trace with validity, reference, and one changed commercial condition.

units.understand: Separate a zero-price customer delivery from a normal sale, credit memo, and free-goods pricing condition.
units.apply: Trace its logistics steps and identify where the absence of customer revenue changes the commercial flow but not the physical flow.
units.explain: Explain why free of charge does not mean no logistics or accounting consequence.
units.evidence: One free-of-charge example compared with standard sell-from-stock and a financial-only correction.

units.primary_label: Sales Process Atlas — Sales Contract Management
units.understand: Understand quantity/value agreements, validity, release orders, consumption, and completion without treating a contract as a normal executable order.
units.apply: Create a release-order scenario and calculate how target and open value or quantity change.
units.explain: Explain what the contract controls and what the release order still has to determine and execute.
units.evidence: A contract/release flow plus one overrun or expiry scenario.

units.primary_label: Sales Automation and Analytics — AI boundary
units.understand: Separate AI assistance, extracted proposals, analytical insight, and ERP transaction authority.
units.apply: Take one AI-proposed order entry and identify evidence, SAP determinations, missing values, and validation before creation.
units.explain: Explain where AI can assist Sales and where business rules, authorization, and transaction state remain authoritative.
units.evidence: A proposal-versus-posted-state comparison and one rejected or ambiguous case.

units.understand: Understand procedure assignment, missing-field detection, status groups, and downstream consequence instead of treating incompleteness as a generic block.
units.apply: Compare two missing fields with different follow-on consequences.
units.explain: Explain how incompleteness differs from delivery blocks, credit blocks, and missing output.
units.evidence: A missing-field trace from document level to the affected follow-on step.

units.official_title: Describing Copy Control for Sales Documents
units.understand: Understand source-target relationships, requirements, transfer logic, reference status, completion, and redetermination.
units.apply: Trace one quotation-to-order or delivery-to-billing copy and change one source value.
units.explain: Explain why a valid predecessor does not guarantee a valid successor.
units.evidence: A source-target comparison with one copied field and one recalculated field.

units.official_title: Configuring Sales Pricing in SAP S/4HANA Cloud
units.understand: Understand pricing procedure, condition type, access sequence, condition record, calculation base, scales, and condition interaction as separate layers.
units.apply: Work one price with base price, percentage discount, and scale; then remove one condition and trace why it disappears.
units.explain: Explain the pricing result from procedure row to record and calculation without reciting transactions.
units.evidence: A worked price plus a missing-condition trace with the exact failed layer.

units.official_title: Processing and Configuring Output in Sales Processes
units.understand: Understand output relevance, output type, receiver, channel, form, and transmission as separate Public Edition decisions.
units.apply: Trace an order confirmation that exists but is not sent and identify the first missing output decision.
units.explain: Explain why document creation, output determination, and transmission are different states.
units.evidence: One output trace distinguishing determination failure from transmission failure.

units.understand: Understand the two legal entities, external customer relationship, delivering company, and separate customer and intercompany billing relationships.
units.apply: Trace one order where one company sells and another company-code plant delivers; mark external and internal invoices separately.
units.explain: Explain why one customer sale creates two commercial relationships and which entity performs each step.
units.evidence: A legal-entity/document-flow diagram separating customer billing from intercompany billing.

units.primary_label: Sales Process Atlas — Advanced Intercompany Sales
units.understand: Understand why 5D2 adds intercompany purchasing/sales documents, value-chain orchestration, valuated stock in transit, and invoice verification.
units.apply: Compare 5D2 with 1HO for the same customer demand and identify every extra internal document and control-transfer event.
units.explain: Explain why advanced intercompany is a different operating model, not merely another invoice.
units.evidence: A 1HO-versus-5D2 comparison showing generated documents, VSiT/control transfer, and settlement.

units.official_title: Sales Processing using Third-Party without Shipping Notification
units.primary_label: Sales Process Atlas — Third-Party Order Processing
units.understand: Understand the BDK boundary: supplier direct delivery, no own outbound delivery or goods receipt in the standard flow, and supplier invoice receipt driving customer billing relevance and quantity.
units.apply: Trace sales order → purchase requisition → purchase order → supplier invoice → customer billing and compare it with a shipping-notification variant.
units.explain: Explain why customer billing can become due without an outbound delivery from the selling company.
units.evidence: A BDK flow with supplier-invoice quantity reconciled to customer-billed quantity.

units.primary_label: Sales Process Atlas — Sales Rebate Processing
units.understand: Understand condition contract, eligible business volume, accrual/settlement logic, scales, and final settlement as a post-invoice commercial process.
units.apply: Calculate a simple rebate threshold, identify which billed volume counts, and show how a return or credit changes eligible volume.
units.explain: Explain why invoice pricing and later rebate settlement are related but not the same calculation.
units.evidence: One condition-contract example with business-volume evidence and settlement result.

units.official_title: Sales Order Processing with Customer Down Payment
units.primary_label: Sales Process Atlas — Customer Down Payment
units.understand: Separate the down-payment request from actual cash receipt and final invoice settlement; understand the billing-plan milestone that drives the request.
units.apply: Trace request → FI noted item → incoming down payment → delivery/performance → final invoice/clearing and mark where cash is actually received.
units.explain: Explain why down-payment request created does not mean customer has paid.
units.evidence: A milestone example with requested amount, received cash, and final clearing.

units.official_title: Sales Order Processing with Invoice List and Collective Billing
units.primary_label: Sales Process Atlas — Collective Billing and Invoice Lists
units.understand: Distinguish collective billing, invoice split, and invoice list: merging billable references is not the same as grouping existing invoices for a payer.
units.apply: Use three deliveries with different header values to predict collective invoice versus split, then group eligible invoices into an invoice list.
units.explain: Explain the object boundary between collective billing and invoice lists without using them as synonyms.
units.evidence: A before/after document-count example naming the field causing any split.

units.primary_label: Sales Process Atlas — Sales Payment Overlay
units.understand: Understand payment authorization/token/reference, Sales context, billing/FI handoff, clearing, and refund traceability as a payment overlay rather than credit management.
units.apply: Trace one authorized payment and one failed or reversed payment, showing who owns authorization and who owns the receivable.
units.explain: Explain the difference between payment authorization, customer credit decision, and financial clearing.
units.evidence: An authorization-to-clearing trace with one failure or reversal path.

units.official_title: Understanding Complaint Management Roles and Responsibilities
units.understand: Classify the requested outcome first: financial correction, physical return, replacement, inspection/disposition, or a combination.
units.apply: For three complaints choose the process owner and first document without turning every complaint into a return.
units.explain: Explain how the business outcome determines the complaint process family.
units.evidence: A triage table showing owner, physical movement, financial movement, and evidence.

units.understand: Understand credit memo request, debit memo request, invoice correction, reference, billing, and FI effect without assuming goods must move.
units.apply: Model an overcharge and an undercharge against an existing invoice and identify the correction path.
units.explain: Explain when a complaint is financial only and why that differs from a return.
units.evidence: A reference-document trace for one credit and one debit correction.

units.understand: Understand return order, receipt, inspection/disposition, logistical follow-up, and refund/replacement decisions as separate states.
units.apply: Trace damaged goods from return authorization to final disposition and financial outcome.
units.explain: Explain why goods receipt, inspection decision, and refund are separate states.
units.evidence: A reverse-logistics flow with disposition and refund evidence.

units.primary_label: Sales Process Atlas — Lean Customer Returns
units.understand: Understand the simpler physical-return flow and its boundary versus the fuller returns-management process.
units.apply: Compare one lean return with one inspected/disposition-based return and state what control steps change.
units.explain: Explain when the lean process is sufficient and what it does not model.
units.evidence: A BKP-versus-BDD comparison with physical and financial states.

units.official_title: Understanding SAP S/4HANA Cloud Returns Analytics
units.understand: Understand returns analytics as observation of return performance and reasons, not execution of the return itself.
units.apply: Take one return metric and trace it back to underlying process documents and reason/disposition data.
units.explain: Explain the difference between operational processing evidence and analytical aggregation.
units.evidence: One metric-to-document trace.

units.understand: Understand the billing-source boundary: eligible external billing data can enter billing without becoming a sales order or delivery.
units.apply: Trace one external billing source to the billing due list and identify compatibility conditions before combining with internal billing items.
units.explain: Explain what is converging and at which billing boundary.
units.evidence: A source-to-billing-object trace.

units.official_title: Using Sales Order Fulfillment Monitoring and Operations
units.understand: Understand exception-based monitoring across order, supply, delivery, invoicing, and accounting phases and separate observation from action.
units.apply: Pick one issue, locate its first unresolved phase, then identify the document and role that owns the next action.
units.explain: Explain how fulfillment monitoring differs from KPI reporting and process execution.
units.evidence: A monitored issue with phase, owner, action, and post-action evidence.

units.primary_label: Sales Automation and Analytics — AI Order Entry
units.understand: Separate extracted or proposed order data from SAP determinations, completeness, authorization, and the created sales order.
units.apply: Review one extracted request, identify uncertain or missing values, and compare the proposal with the final order.
units.explain: Explain why extraction success is not transaction success.
units.evidence: A proposal-versus-created-order field comparison.

units.understand: Understand sales plans as targets by period and dimensions, distinct from orders, predictions, and actual analytical results.
units.apply: Create a small plan grain and compare plan versus actual for one customer/product dimension.
units.explain: Explain the difference between planning a target and predicting or observing an outcome.
units.evidence: A plan/actual comparison with explicit grain and period.

units.official_title: Using SAP Fiori Analytical Apps for Sales
units.understand: Understand analytical questions, dimensions, measures, filters, drill-down, and the source business state behind a KPI.
units.apply: Take one analytical result and reconcile it to underlying documents or its aggregation boundary.
units.explain: Explain what the analysis proves and what it cannot prove about current execution.
units.evidence: A KPI-to-document reconciliation.

units.official_title: Describing Predictive Analytics Model Training - Sales
units.understand: Understand training data, target variable, model version, quality indicators, activation, and prediction as different from reporting or planning.
units.apply: Describe the training/activation lifecycle and how stale or biased historical data affects predictions.
units.explain: Explain why a prediction is evidence for a decision, not a committed business transaction.
units.evidence: A model-lifecycle explanation plus one data-quality risk.
